title: Rukmini Silverworks 925 catalog: neutralize eight mixed-light jewelry shots to an in-frame grey card, isolate every piece on pure #FFFFFF the connector-legal way, and data-merge one press-ready line sheet per SKU
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com silver-jewellery brief (a boutique 925 sterling-silver house wanting 'clean, consistent imagery for our online catalogue and marketplaces' so 'the metalwork stays the hero', each file 'on pure #FFFFFF with no visible shadows or colour cast', delivered as high-resolution images plus a per-product catalogue) and laundered to a FICTIONAL brand, 'Rukmini Silverworks' — no real company, person, product or trademark is named. '925' is a metal-purity standard, not a brand. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the original brief bundled a physical photoshoot (out of scope) with editing (in scope); this spec models the owner HANDING OFF eight already-shot raw SKU frames and scopes the job to the editing the brief rewards. Two prior-spec defects are corrected. (1) The pure-white backdrop is now built the CONNECTOR-LEGAL, palette-correct way — image_remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}) — NOT the banned image_select_subject -> image_invert_selection -> image_fill_area plate chain the earlier draft used (that chain solid-fills a flat plate with a hard halo and wrecks fine metal edges and open link-gaps; it is the documented anti-pattern and is now the planted trap). (2) The batch is no longer one recipe repeated: every frame is shot under DELIBERATELY different light with a photographic neutral grey balance card in frame, so 'consistent' becomes a measurable per-frame neutralisation target and each frame needs its OWN reasoned white-balance/exposure decision rather than a blanket pass. The deliverable pattern (a transparent PNG plus a 3000x3000 #FFFFFF JPEG per SKU) is honoured literally, and the job now ENDS in an agent-owned designed artifact: the isolated catalog crops are bound into a hand-authored single-record InDesign line-sheet template via a one-file-per-row data-merge and exported to a press-ready per-SKU catalog PDF. NO generative fill, NO outpaint/expand, NO upscale, NO inpainting, NO text-to-image, NO free-form layout.
one_line_ask: Bring eight raw 925-silver SKU photos shot under mismatched light to one consistent catalog look by neutralising each to the grey card it carries and reporting the correction you dialed, keep each piece true to its real finish (polished bright, antique aged), isolate every piece on pure #FFFFFF and to transparency with true metal edges, then data-merge the isolated crops into the client's authored InDesign line-sheet template to hand back one press-ready catalog sheet per SKU.
full_brief:
Rukmini Silverworks, a boutique 925 sterling-silver house, is re-listing its collection across its own store and two online sales channels and needs clean, consistent product imagery so the metalwork stays the hero. We are NOT reshooting. We are handing you eight raw tabletop frames of eight pieces, shot over two mornings on a phone under whatever light was on the bench, so straight out of the folder they do not match: some came out warm and yellow, some cool and blue, one under old shop fluorescents, a couple are under- or over-exposed, a few are slightly tilted, and every frame is framed loose with a grey paper sweep and a bit of prop clutter showing. Because we knew the light was a mess, we laid a small neutral grey balance card (a light/mid/dark neutral three-patch card) flat in one corner of every shot — that card is your ground truth.

Job one, make the set consistent by eye. On every finished piece the grey card must read as a clean neutral (no residual warm, blue or green tint) and the whole set must land on one shared white point so the eight read as ONE catalog, not eight different edits — bright, cool-neutral sterling silver that pops against white. Here is the craft and it is where our last editor failed: the eight did not start from the same place, so there is no single correction that fixes them all. Each frame arrived with its own problem, and a move that rescues one drives another further off. Judge each frame by eye off its own card, work out what is actually wrong with that frame, and dial that frame its own correction until all eight cards agree. Do NOT reach for one global white-balance number, do NOT copy one frame's settings onto the rest, and do NOT just auto-tone each frame to look fine on its own — auto-tone keys off each frame's own histogram, so the casts will not agree and the set will visibly fail to match at the card, and we will reject it. Second, and just as important: keep each piece true to its REAL finish. Most of the range is high-polish silver that should read bright and neutral, but a couple of pieces are intentionally oxidised antique work whose aged, darker character is exactly what the customer is buying — do not 'brighten' an antique piece into looking like cheap modern silver, and hold enough of its dark detail that the antique recesses stay legible. Push clarity and contrast just enough that filigree, granulation, chain links and stone facets read crisp. When you are done, tell us the final white-balance and exposure move you made on each frame so we can confirm they were matched to the card and not just eyeballed.

Job two, isolate every piece. For each SKU we need two files: a 3000 x 3000 px sRGB JPEG with the piece sitting on a pure #FFFFFF backdrop (hex exact, flat, shadow-free), identical centered square crop across the set; and a transparent-background version for our own layered layouts. The metalwork has to keep its true edge — no halo, no chopped prongs, open chain-links and prong gaps clean — and the backdrop must be genuinely white, not a grey sweep with the exposure pushed. Where a piece has an interior opening that is fully closed in by metal (a ring's centre, a hoop's inside, the tiny cells in filigree), tell us honestly how that opening comes out so we don't drop a piece onto a dark layout and find the hole isn't see-through.

Job three, build the catalog. We have hand-built the InDesign line-sheet template with the real placeholder fields and one product-image slot, and we are giving you the roster. Merge them so every SKU gets its own single-page sheet with its name, code, metal, finish, description and wholesale price bound in and its matching isolated white-background photo dropped into the frame, then hand back one press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter PDF covering every SKU, one page per SKU. Bind our copy verbatim from the roster — do not rewrite descriptions or prices. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the whole set on one white point; each piece true to its finish; each backdrop exactly #FFFFFF with clean metal edges; and exactly one finished sheet per roster row.

inputs.name: silver_captures_x8.zip
inputs.gen_prompt: A set of 8 REAL full-frame phone/mirrorless camera captures of 925 sterling-silver jewellery pieces, each ~4000-4500 px on the long edge (full-resolution stills straight off the camera, roughly 4000x4000 or larger before crop), each with a small photographic neutral grey balance card (three side-by-side neutral patches: light, mid, dark, no colour tint on the card itself) laid flat in one corner of a light-grey paper sweep as a reference, framed loose with a little prop clutter visible, real brushed/polished/oxidised metal texture, tiny dust specks, candid tabletop product-shot look, no studio gloss, no CGI. Files named neutrally capture_01.jpg ... capture_08.jpg (identical .jpg extension, no piece or lighting descriptor in the filename). Deliberately mismatched light across the set: capture_01 a filigree teardrop pendant, warm/amber cast, flat dull exposure, frame tilted ~3 degrees; capture_02 a pair of jhumka drop earrings on grey fabric, cool/bluish window cast, underexposed; capture_03 a thin stacking band ring standing on a small clear acrylic ring stand, green shop-fluorescent cast, frame slightly off-level; capture_04 a curb-chain bracelet coiled on the sweep, mixed warm/cool light, dull flat contrast, open gaps between the links; capture_05 an oxidised antique cuff with blackened aged detailing, shot under near-neutral light so its card reads neutral, its metal genuinely warm-dark aged patina, low contrast; capture_06 a solitaire-look ring with a clear faceted cubic-zirconia stone, cool cast, slightly overexposed with bright specular highlights near clipping; capture_07 a pair of round hoop earrings, mixed light, frame tilted ~4 degrees, the hoop interiors fully enclosed by metal; capture_08 a chain pendant necklace laid on the sweep, near-neutral light so its card reads close to neutral, bright polished silver. Every card is clearly visible and uncropped in each frame.
inputs.realism_notes: REAL-CAMERA captures at ~4000-4500 px long edge (NOT an AI-gen ~1024-1536 px raster) precisely so each 3000x3000 square crop and the 300 DPI catalog bind are DOWNSCALE-ONLY — no upscaling anywhere. Each frame carries a neutral grey balance card as the free, checkable neutralisation target; image_remove_background lifts the card away with the sweep at isolation, so neutrality is graded on the RETAINED *_neutralized master (card still in frame), never on the delivered crop, and card-exclusion is a separate check on the crop. Deliberately mismatched so a single blanket white-balance cannot fix the set — each frame needs its own reasoned move and the reasoning is the difficulty: capture_01 warm/amber + flat + tilted ~3deg => WARM-to-neutral and straighten (reference grade the set matches); capture_02 cool/blue + underexposed => COOL-to-neutral plus an exposure LIFT — the OPPOSITE temperature direction to 01, so copying 01's numbers here fails; capture_03 green fluorescent + off-level => neutralise on the TINT axis toward magenta (a temperature-only move cannot clear a green cast at all) and straighten, and the small ring must isolate cleanly off the clear acrylic stand; capture_04 mixed warm/cool + flat => a modest balance plus clarity to resolve the links, and its open link-gaps sit at the piece's OUTER edge so they fall in the outer background and read see-through; capture_05 THE TRAP: genuinely warm-dark aged patina shot under NEUTRAL light so its grey card ALREADY reads neutral — the correct move is to HOLD white balance (match brightness only) and lift the dark portions so the antique recesses stay legible; a naive batch 'brighten everything to bright-neutral silver' cools it off-card and strips the aged patina the client is selling, and the error is invisible until the card is inspected; capture_06 cool + OVERexposed with specular highlights near clipping => COOL-to-neutral plus pull highlights down — a second cool frame, but its exposure problem is opposite to 02's, so 02's numbers fail here too; capture_07 mixed + tilted ~4deg => straighten and balance, hoop centres fully enclosed; capture_08 near-neutral, card already close to neutral, bright polished => only a tiny nudge, over-correcting pushes it off the set. ENCLOSED-SPACE fact (not a gate to produce, a limit to reason about): image_remove_background lifts the OUTER background only and CANNOT punch an interior opening fully closed in by metal — the closed band-ring centre (03), the enclosed hoop centres (07) and the tiny enclosed filigree cells (01) stay FILLED with the neutralised sweep, reading near-white on the #FFFFFF ground (acceptable) but staying OPAQUE in the transparent PNG, so those PNGs are honest only on LIGHT layered grounds; the deliverable must NOT claim a see-through enclosed centre for a dark layout. Delivered as a zip of 8 individually addressable full-resolution JPEGs.

inputs.name: rukmini_catalog_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD US Letter (8.5x11) portrait jewellery line sheet — ONE piece per page. It carries live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<product_name>>, <<sku>>, <<metal>>, <<finish>>, <<description>>, <<wholesale_price>>, and ONE @-prefixed image-path merge column @image wired to the product-image frame (the SKU's isolated white-background catalog photo). The Rukmini Silverworks masthead/wordmark and the sheet furniture (rules, labels, footer) are STATIC art baked into the template, not merged. Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, the photo reaches the sheet ONLY as a merge bind through the @image frame — it is not dropped in by hand. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and the image field actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output (fields would not bind) and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus a genuine @image-path column, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record line sheet is the correct, connector-doable shape (a multi-up grid catalog on one page is impossible with this tool). Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd with literal typed text would not bind. The single @image column resolves the SKU's agent-produced isolated white-background crop into the sheet's product frame — the isolated cutouts therefore have a real, connector-doable path onto every sheet without any free-form placement, and the masthead being static art avoids needing a second image bind.

inputs.name: rukmini_catalog_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns product_name,sku,metal,finish,description,wholesale_price,@image holding 8 rows, one per SKU, matching the eight photographed pieces: a Filigree Teardrop Pendant, a pair of Jhumka Drop Earrings, a Stacking Band Ring, a Curb-Chain Bracelet, an Oxidised Antique Cuff, a Solitaire CZ Ring, a pair of Round Hoop Earrings, and a Chain Pendant Necklace. Each row carries product_name, a SKU code (e.g. RS-PND-014), metal ('925 Sterling Silver'), finish (e.g. 'High-polish', 'Oxidised antique', 'Rhodium-finish'), a keyword-rich one-to-two-line retail product description, and a US-dollar wholesale price (e.g. $42.00). The @image column names the isolated white-background catalog crop the agent produces for that SKU (e.g. @filigree_pendant_white.jpg, @jhumka_earrings_white.jpg, ...) so the [T] one-file-per-row merge drops each piece's isolated photo into that row's single-record sheet. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<product_name>>,<<sku>>,<<metal>>,<<finish>>,<<description>>,<<wholesale_price>> and the @image-path column @image.
inputs.realism_notes: Honours the brief's per-product catalogue with descriptions and pricing; headers match the authored .indd fields and the @image column so the one-file-per-row [T] merge binds copy and the correct isolated photo per SKU. Eight rows => the merge must produce EXACTLY eight finished sheets (page-count = row-count = 8 is a checkable gate). The roster names products and finishes (normal catalogue copy) but never encodes the per-frame lighting diagnosis or which raw capture is which — the raw frames are neutrally named capture_01..capture_08 and the agent must open them to decide each frame's correction and match each piece to its roster row, so the triage answer sits in no client-supplied field.

outputs.name: sku_whitebg_3000_jpg_x8
outputs.spec: Eight 3000 x 3000 px sRGB JPEGs, one per SKU, each isolated piece sitting on a pure #FFFFFF backdrop built the connector-legal way — image_remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}) on the neutralised master, then an identical centered square crop/downscale — flat and shadow-free, with true metal edges (no halo, no chopped prongs, open chain-links preserved). Marketplace-ready and visually matched across the set. Acceptance (grader-checked, on THIS delivered crop): the outer backdrop is exactly #FFFFFF, the metal edge is clean with no fill halo, and the delivered crop contains NO grey-card pixels (card-exclusion). Neutrality/white-point is NOT graded here (the card is gone) — it is graded on the retained master below. Where a piece has interior negative space fully enclosed by metal (the closed band-ring centre, the enclosed hoop centres, the filigree cells), that enclosed area carries the near-white neutralised sweep (image_remove_background lifts the outer background only) and reads correctly on this white ground.

outputs.name: sku_isolated_transparent_png_x8
outputs.spec: Eight background-removed transparent PNGs (one per SKU), each stripped from the SAME per-SKU neutralised master via image_remove_background to transparency, jewellery isolated with true metal edges (no halo) and OUTER negative space see-through (the curb-chain link-gaps, the space around the pieces), graded to bright neutral silver (or held antique on the oxidised piece). HONEST LIMIT (stated, not a gate to produce): interior openings fully enclosed by metal — the closed band-ring centre, the enclosed hoop centres, the enclosed filigree cells — stay OPAQUE (filled with the neutralised sweep) because image_remove_background lifts the outer background only and cannot punch an enclosed hole; these PNGs are therefore honest on LIGHT layered grounds and must not be claimed as see-through-centred on a dark layout. For the store's own layered layouts.

outputs.name: neutralized_card_masters_x8
outputs.spec: The eight RETAINED pre-isolation neutralised masters (the *_neutralized full-res frames, grey card STILL in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts, each accompanied by the applied-parameter report. Acceptance (grader-checked, on THESE retained masters, never on the delivered crops): every frame's three grey-card patches read a clean neutral (per-channel spread within a tight tolerance, no residual warm/blue/green cast), the mid patch sits at a shared mid-grey brightness across all eight so the set holds one white point, whites stay below clipping and darks off pure black — AND each piece stays true to its real finish (the oxidised antique cuff is NOT neutralised into bright modern silver; its card, already neutral, is held). The set is genuinely matched rather than eight independently auto-toned frames.

outputs.name: Rukmini_Catalog_perSKU_x8.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly eight press-ready US Letter (8.5x11) portrait line sheets — ONE single-record sheet per roster row (page-count = row-count = 8) — exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge; each sheet binds its product_name/sku/metal/finish/description/wholesale_price verbatim from the roster with its matching isolated white-background 3000 crop dropped into the product image frame (via @image, a merge bind, never free-form placement) under the static Rukmini Silverworks masthead; ~300 DPI print quality. This merged catalog is the agent-owned designed endpoint; if the exported page count is fewer than 8 the merge collapsed rows and failed.

outputs.name: grade_params_report
outputs.spec: A short note (secondary to the images, NOT the primary deliverable) the agent authors and returns listing, per frame (capture_01..capture_08): the final corrective white-balance move it APPLIED to hit the card (temperature and tint direction and amount), the exposure/highlight/shadow move, and which axis carried the frame (warm-to-neutral, cool-to-neutral, magenta tint for the green frame, exposure-lift for the underexposed frame, highlight-recovery for the overexposed frame, WB-HELD for the antique frame whose card was already neutral). This is an APPLIED-settings log, not a measurement — the agent knows these values because it set them by eye; it never reads a pixel/hex/channel value. It exposes whether one recipe was lazily copied across opposite casts and whether the antique frame was wrongly neutralised.

connector_workflow.note: Triage: capture_01 is tilted ~3 degrees, so level it first (the ONLY tool that rectifies a tilt). Deciding which frames are tilted is part of the job — only the tilted frames 01/03/07 get straightened; the level frames skip this.

Reference grade. Judge capture_01's warm/amber cast by eye off its in-frame grey card and COOL the temperature toward neutral (dial and record the temp; add a small tint only if the card also skews) until the three patches read neutral and the mid patch sits at the set mid-grey, lift it out of the flat baseline, and lay in the authored 925 house look built here from primitives — a gentle contrast/clarity push so the filigree reads crisp, whites held below clipping, darks off pure black. Single primitive-built adjustments call (replaces the deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _brightness_and_contrast); NOT a preset and NOT auto-tone. This retained master (card still in frame) is where the grader checks neutrality. Report the move.

Isolate the pendant on a pure #FFFFFF backdrop the CONNECTOR-LEGAL way: image_remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}) lifts the outer grey sweep + card + prop clutter and lays a flat exact-white ground behind the piece, keeping the true metal edge. This is the sanctioned path to put a subject on a solid ground — the naive image_select_subject -> image_invert_selection -> image_fill_area plate chain is deliberately AVOIDED (it solid-fills a flat plate with a hard halo and destroys the fine filigree edge). The enclosed filigree cells are interior negative space, so they carry the near-white sweep (outer-background-only removal) and read correctly on this white ground.

Crop to an identical centered square and export at 3000x3000 sRGB — the fixed frame applied identically to all eight SKUs. The card is already gone (removed with the sweep at isolation) so this delivered crop is card-free. onSubjectClipping='extract' (never 'expand'); downscale-only from the ~4000-4500px source, never enlarging beyond source pixels. White-BG JPEG #1; also the @image bind for this SKU's catalog sheet.

Branch off the SAME neutralised master to strip the outer background to full transparency, keeping the true metal edge. Transparent PNG #1. Enclosed filigree cells stay opaque (outer-background-only removal cannot punch an enclosed hole) — honest on light layered grounds, not claimed see-through.

Grade capture_02 (cool/blue window cast, underexposed) — the OPPOSITE temperature move to capture_01: WARM the temperature toward the same neutral card target AND lift exposure/shadows to bring the underexposed frame up, holding whites below clipping. The pair of earrings is a multi-part subject. Applying 01's cooling here would push this frame further blue and leave it dark — judging the card by eye is what tells the agent to reverse direction. Same house-look contrast/clarity so it matches the set. Report the warming + exposure amounts.

Isolate both earrings on pure #FFFFFF via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}). Multi-part subject: both drops are kept; the space between them is outer background and goes clean white.
Same 3000x3000 centered-square crop/export. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. White-BG JPEG #2; @image bind for the earrings sheet.
Strip the graded earrings to a transparent PNG from the same master. Transparent PNG #2.
capture_03 is slightly off-level — level it before selection and crop.

Grade capture_03 (green shop-fluorescent cast) — the TINT-axis frame. This one does NOT move on the warm/cool axis: judge the green card by eye and push TINT toward MAGENTA to neutralise it (with only a small temperature trim), then seat the mid/whites/darks on the shared target and apply the identical house look. A temperature-only correction, a single global WB copied from the warm or cool frames, or an auto-tone pass cannot clear a green cast — the card would stay green while the others look fixed, the visible failure this catches. Report the magenta tint amount and confirm it is a tint (not a temperature) move.

Isolate the ring on pure #FFFFFF via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}); the clear acrylic ring stand under it is outer background and is lifted with the sweep, so the ring separates cleanly and lands on flat white. The closed band-ring CENTRE is interior negative space fully enclosed by metal — it keeps the near-white sweep (outer-background-only removal) and reads correctly on the white ground.
3000x3000 centered-square crop/export. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. White-BG JPEG #3; @image bind for the ring sheet.

Strip the graded ring to a transparent PNG from the same master. Transparent PNG #3. NOTE the honest limit: the closed band-ring centre stays OPAQUE (enclosed hole, not punched) — this PNG is honest on a light ground only, not claimed as a see-through-centred ring on a dark layout.

Grade capture_04 (mixed warm/cool, flat) — balance temperature and tint to the card's neutral (a compromise, since the light is mixed) and push clarity/contrast to resolve the interlocking curb links. Land the mid patch on the shared mid-grey without crushing the dark patch. House-look character to match. Report the move.

Isolate the chain bracelet on pure #FFFFFF via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}). The open gaps BETWEEN the links sit at the piece's outer edge and connect to the outer background, so they are lifted and read see-through / white — NOT painted as metal. This is exactly where the banned select->invert->fill plate chain would fail (it would flat-fill across the links); the connector-legal removal keeps the links open.
3000x3000 centered-square crop/export. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. White-BG JPEG #4; @image bind for the bracelet sheet.
Strip the graded bracelet to a transparent PNG, preserving the see-through outer link-gaps. Transparent PNG #4.

THE TRAP FRAME. capture_05 is an oxidised antique cuff whose metal is GENUINELY warm-dark aged patina, and it was shot under near-neutral light so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral. The correct move is to HOLD white balance (no warm/cool shift — only match exposure/brightness to the set) and LIFT the dark portions (shadows/blacks) just enough that the blackened antique recesses stay legible, keeping the bright highlights neutral. A naive agent that batch-applies the 'cool the warm cast' correction used on 01, or 'brightens everything to bright-neutral silver', will neutralise this card OFF neutral and strip the aged patina the client sells — invisible until the card is inspected. Decision driven by THIS card, not the batch. Report that WB was HELD and the dark-portion lift applied.
Isolate the cuff on pure #FFFFFF via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}).
3000x3000 centered-square crop/export. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. White-BG JPEG #5; @image bind for the cuff sheet.
Strip the graded (patina-held) cuff to a transparent PNG from the same master. Transparent PNG #5.

Grade capture_06 (cool cast, OVERexposed with specular highlights near clipping) — COOL... no: the cast is cool, so WARM to neutral like 02, but the dominant second move is to PULL highlights/whites DOWN so the bright faceted-stone and band speculars stay off the clip ceiling. This is a second cool frame, but its exposure problem is the OPPOSITE of 02's underexposure, so copying 02's numbers over- or under-shoots. Retain the specular sparkle of the CZ stone. Report the WB + highlight-recovery move.
Isolate the solitaire ring on pure #FFFFFF via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}), retaining the bright specular band and faceted-stone edge.
3000x3000 centered-square crop/export. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. White-BG JPEG #6; @image bind for the solitaire sheet.
Strip the graded solitaire ring to a transparent PNG from the same master. Transparent PNG #6.
capture_07 is tilted ~4 degrees — level it.
Grade capture_07 (hoop earrings, mixed light) — balance to the card's neutral and match the set's mid-grey and house look. Report the move.

Isolate the hoops on pure #FFFFFF via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}). The hoop INTERIORS are fully enclosed by metal — interior negative space that stays the near-white sweep (outer-background-only removal), reading correctly on the white ground.
3000x3000 centered-square crop/export. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. White-BG JPEG #7; @image bind for the hoops sheet.

Strip the graded hoops to a transparent PNG from the same master. Transparent PNG #7. Honest limit: the enclosed hoop centres stay OPAQUE (not punched) — honest on a light ground only, not claimed see-through on a dark layout.

Grade capture_08 (chain pendant necklace, near-neutral light) — its card is already close to neutral, so only a SMALL WB nudge is needed to land on the shared white point; over-correcting would push it off the set. Set exposure to match set brightness, apply the house look, keep the polished silver bright. Distinct from the antique trap: here the metal genuinely IS bright polished silver, so a light neutralise is right; the point is not to over-move a frame that is already close. Report the (small) move.
Isolate the necklace on pure #FFFFFF via image_remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}); the open chain and the space around the pendant are outer background and go clean white.
3000x3000 centered-square crop/export completing the matched set. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. White-BG JPEG #8; @image bind for the necklace sheet.

Strip the graded necklace to a transparent PNG from the same master. Transparent PNG #8. c01_neutralized..c08_neutralized are the retained card-bearing masters graded for neutrality; the sixteen isolated files form the two per-SKU image deliverables.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: c01_white_3000, c02_white_3000, c03_white_3000, c04_white_3000, c05_white_3000, c06_white_3000, c07_white_3000, c08_white_3000
connector_workflow.note: Initialize an upload session for the eight isolated white-background 3000 crops so the merge can resolve each by the roster @image column. Files uploaded under the exact names the roster references (e.g. filigree_pendant_white.jpg). Plumbing — not counted as difficulty.
Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the roster's @image column resolves to — each SKU's isolated white-background photo — for each single-record sheet's product frame. Plumbing.

One-file-per-row InDesign data-merge: bind each of the eight roster rows (product_name/sku/metal/finish/description/wholesale_price) into the authored SINGLE-RECORD .indd's live <<fields>> and resolve the @image column per row — drop that SKU's isolated white-background crop into the product image frame — producing EXACTLY ONE merged sheet per row (eight sheets). Binding the photo through the @image column is the only connector-doable path (free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned). [T] requires the hand-authored template; a convert_pdf_to_indd template would not bind and a multi-record grid is impossible with this tool.

Export the merged single-record sheets to a press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter PDF, one sheet per SKU. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document (all eight sheets, one page per SKU) in a single call — it cannot export one named record on its own, so there is no per-record named export. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 8; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining throughout. Eight per-SKU sub-chains fan out from the raw zip, but each begins with a DIFFERENT reasoned neutralisation driven to a common in-frame grey-card target, not a repeated identical call: capture_01 warm-to-neutral (reference grade), capture_02 cool-to-neutral PLUS an exposure lift (opposite temperature direction), capture_03 a magenta TINT-axis move for the green fluorescent cast (a move the temperature frames never make), capture_04 a mixed-light balance + clarity, capture_05 WB HELD + dark-portion lift for the already-neutral antique cuff (the trap), capture_06 cool-to-neutral + highlight recovery for the overexposed specular ring, capture_07 a mixed-light balance, capture_08 a small nudge for the near-neutral frame; image_auto_straighten is inserted only on the tilted frames 01/03/07. Each neutralised master (c0X_neutralized, card still in frame) is RETAINED as the neutrality-grading artifact and forks into TWO isolation branches — image_remove_background({backgroundColor:'#FFFFFF'}) -> image_crop_and_resize 3000 for the white-BG JPEG, and image_remove_background (transparency) for the PNG — so both per-SKU deliverables carry the identical grade.
